chapter.title: Far and Near
chapter.tagline: Mastering measurement units: millimetres, centimetres, metres, and kilometres
chapter.overview: Cheenu and Deepu learn to choose appropriate metric units for everyday items—from tiny ant legs (mm) to pencil lengths (cm), classroom walls (m), and city distances (km). They read scaled rulers and translate map scales into real distances.

storyNarrative.dialogue: My crayon is past 6 cm and reaches 4 small tick marks. That means it is 6 cm and 4 mm, or 6.4 cm!

concept.heading: Decimal Subdivisions of Centimetres
concept.keyRule: Each millimetre mark is one-tenth (0.1) of a centimetre.

sections.title: Map Scales: Centimetres on Paper to Kilometres on Ground
sections.subtitle: Translating ratio scales (e.g. 1 cm = 100 km)

storyNarrative.dialogue: On this map, the scale says 1 cm represents 100 km. If the distance between two towns is 3.5 cm on the paper, how far is it in real life?

concept.heading: Proportional Scaling
concept.keyRule: Real Distance = Map Measurement × Scale Factor (3.5 cm × 100 km/cm = 350 km).
